title: Microsegmented procurement experiments for specialty LLMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Run a small battery of targeted field experiments to validate procurement signals (integration friction, latency sensitivity, quantization tolerance, and license/legal constraints) for narrow/specialty LLMs used by enterprise verticals. The goal is to translate noisy marketplace signals into actionable procurement heuristics and a scorecard that sales/solutions teams can use when evaluating a model supplier or deciding between hosted vs reserved capacity.

Context: We’ve historically tracked macro model availability and performance, but customers buying for regulated verticals (finserv/legal/healthcare) make decisions based on integration effort, quantization compatibility, and licensing small-print. This ticket seeds experiments that measure those dimensions empirically with artifacted evidence (benchmarks, integration notes, cost deltas).

Scope: 3-week field-lab running 6 micro-experiments across representative enterprise workloads: short-context summarization, secure-RAG, high-throughput embeddings, multi-turn chat with tool-calls, re-ranking for search, and domain-specific Q&A. For each model candidate, capture: integration steps and blockers, quantization artifacts and accuracy delta, median P95 latency at target concurrency, estimated infra cost change (tokens and GPU-hour proxy), and license/TOU red flags.

Deliverables:
- A reproducible microbench harness (scripts + container) that can run each experiment against multiple models and generate standardized CSV outputs.
- A procurement scorecard template with weighted heuristics (integration friction, latency penalty, cost delta, tailoring effort, legal risk).
- A short playbook for field reps describing when to push hosted API vs Dedicated or Private based on score thresholds.
- Dashboard prototype (console widget) showing signal snapshots for model candidates.

Experimental approach:
- Select 6 candidate models: 2 open-source quant-friendly models, 2 larger open variants, and 2 commercial APIs (with permissioned telemetry). Prioritize models flagged by Sales as potential migration targets.
- Build lightweight adapters for each model to standardize prompt/IO and measure per-call latency and token counts.
- Run deterministic workloads derived from anonymized customer prompts and synthetic edge cases to stress integration (e.g., long docs, repeated ephemeral API keys, high-concurrency embedding batches).
- For quantization assessment run the same model after applying the recommended quantization profile and compare quality via embedding similarity and a small labeled QA set.

Metrics (primary):
- Integration friction score (qualitative checklist aggregated into 0-10).
- Quality delta after quantization (relative BLEU/EM/synthetic label F1 or embedding cosine drop).
- P95 latency at target concurrency (ms).
- Cost delta per 1M tokens or per 1k embeddings (USD estimate).
- Legal/license red flags (enumerated list).

Risk & trade-offs:
- Running commercial APIs for benching may breach provider TOU—coordinate with Legal and Sales; where restricted, use synthetic proxies.
- Field tests may not generalize; keep experiments explicitly narrow and document assumptions.
- This project competes for engineering time with runtime optimization work; scope the harness to minimal viable automation and leverage existing benchmarking infra where possible.

Operational notes:
- Use the 'procurement-field-lab' AWS account and isolated datasets (anonymized).
- Store artifacts in the shared GDrive folder and tag PRs with PM-1212121.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Reproducible harness able to run all 6 micro-experiments end-to-end in CI.
- Procurement scorecard populated for the 6 candidates with clear recommendations (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Dashboard prototype with at least 3 tiles (integration friction, latency, cost delta).
- Shareable one-pager and demo to Sales + Solutions with decision rules.

Estimated timeline:
Week 1: model selection, harness scaffold, basic adapters.
Week 2: run experiments, collect artifacts, iterate on metrics.
Week 3: synthesize scorecard, build dashboard prototype, review with stakeholders and finalize playbook.

Notes to reviewers: prioritization decision required on the engineering side for 8 points scope. Ask runtime infra to allocate 2 engineer-days for adapter support. We will reuse the benchmarking infra from PM-303303 where possible.
